events.content: Now I understand the setup: Next 16 canary with `cacheComponents: true`. The title only appears after 800ms today because it's awaited alongside the slow details inside one Suspense boundary, so the whole page is below the shell. Let me restructure so the title is part of the prerendered static shell (which is what a shell-only prefetch delivers).

events.content:
Done. The title now arrives with the prefetched shell, while the rest of the page is left out of the prefetch.

**What was wrong:** the whole page sat inside one Suspense boundary, and `getProjectTitle` was awaited in `Promise.all` with the 800 ms `getProjectDetails` — so the title couldn't render until the slow call finished, and nothing but `Loading project...` was in the shell.

**Changes:**

1. `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` — the page awaits `params` and the title directly, renders `<h1>` in the shell, and moves only the details below a `<Suspense>` boundary.
2. `generateStaticParams` (+ `getProjectSlugs` in `lib/data.ts`) — without it, `params` isn't known at prerender time, so a param-dependent title can never be in a prefetchable shell; it would fall back to the loading state.
3. `await connection()` in `ProjectDetails` — this was the non-obvious part. `getProjectDetails` is `'use cache'`, so with `cacheComponents` the details prerendered *into* the shell and the prefetch carried the entire page. I verified this in the build artifacts: the prefetchable segment contained `Commerce storefront` and `Production deployment`. `connection()` defers that subtree to request time without touching the cache, so it's excluded from the shell but still a cache read.
4. `app/page.tsx` — explicit `prefetch="auto"` on the dashboard links, i.e. shell-only. This is the default, but stating it guards the intent against someone later switching to `prefetch={true}` or `unstable_dynamicOnHover`, either of which would pull the dynamic details in.

**Verified against a production build:**

- Route report went from `○ /projects/acme` (fully static, whole page prefetched) to `◐ /projects/acme` (partial prerender).
- The prefetchable segment (`__PAGE__.segment.rsc`) now contains only `Acme Storefront` + `Loading project`, with no description or activity.
- `next start`: full page renders correctly; cold request 0.91 s, warm 0.02 s, confirming `'use cache'` still works; unknown slugs still render "Unknown project".

One trade-off worth flagging: the details are no longer in the prerendered HTML, so on a cold cache the first request streams them after ~800 ms instead of serving them instantly from a build-time prerender. That's the direct cost of keeping them out of the prefetch — if you'd rather have build-time details for the initial load, drop the `connection()` call, but the prefetch will then include the full page again.

`next build` also rewrote `tsconfig.json` (`jsx: react-jsx`, an added `include` path); I reverted it to keep the diff focused, and it will reappear on your next build.
